name: Citicoline (CDP-choline)
short: Stroke trials: deaths, serious heart events like placebo; high bias risk, safety unknown. Alzheimer's, with cholinesterase inhibitors: occasional self-limiting excitability, stomach upset, headache.
text: A Cochrane review of 10 randomised trials with 4281 people with acute ischaemic stroke (citicoline given by mouth, into a vein, or both) found, in a pooled analysis of eight trials, there may be little or no difference from placebo in deaths from any cause (17.3% versus 18.5%) or, in three trials, in serious cardiovascular adverse events (8.83% versus 7.77%); however, all the trials were at high risk of bias, other adverse events were poorly reported, the reviewers said harms may have been underestimated, and they concluded that the safety profile of citicoline remains unknown. In a large placebo-controlled trial in 2298 patients with moderate-to-severe acute ischaemic stroke, no significant differences were reported in the safety outcomes or in the rate of adverse events; the abstract does not say whether this trial was among those in the Cochrane review. In a 12-week randomised placebo-controlled trial in 100 healthy adults aged 50 to 85 with age-related memory complaints, safety was monitored with adverse-event questions, blood pressure and blood tests, and the authors concluded that citicoline may be safe; the abstract does not report the adverse-event results. A systematic review of two retrospective cohort studies in 563 older people with Alzheimer's disease, who took citicoline added to cholinesterase-inhibitor drugs, described the adverse events of the combination as self-limiting, including occasional excitability, gastric intolerance and headache. No other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
